title: Avancerade digitala färdigheter
description: Förväntat resultat:    Resultat:     Anslutna nationella koalitioner för digital kompetens och digitala arbetstillfällen till kärnplattformen.    Mål:  Plattformen för digital kompetens och digitala arbetstillfällen utgör en gemensam informationspunkt om digitala färdigheter i Europa. På EU-nivå samlar plattformen all relevant information och alla finansieringsmöjligheter som berörda parter kan dra nytta av. På nationell nivå ansluter den till den nationella koalitionens webbplatser och inrättar ett ömsesidigt berikande utbyte med relevant innehåll och data om digitala färdigheter och arbetstillfällen. Under 2024 är 22 nationella webbplatser anslutna till plattformen. Ytterligare webbplatser i medlemsstaterna kommer att kopplas samman genom det pågående projektet om nationella koalitioner för digital kompetens och digitala arbetstillfällen  [1]  senast 2026. Plattformen är också värd för Cyber Security Skills Academy och kommer att vara värd för andra relevanta sektorsakademier och initiativ.  Syftet med detta ämne är att konsolidera och upprätthålla driften av plattformen för digital kompetens och digitala arbetstillfällen, inbegripet korrigerande och anpassningsbart underhåll. Detta ämne kommer också att stödja och utvidga verksamheten i samband med koalitionen för digital kompetens och digitala arbetstillfällen samt fördjupa utbytet mellan den nationella koalitionens webbplatser och den centrala plattformen. Detta ämne syftar till att ytterligare öka antalet nationella koalitioner, få befintliga och nya nationella koalitioner att bli mer aktiva och engagerade och öka antalet medlemmar i koalitionen för digital kompetens och digitala arbetstillfällen. Synergieffekter bör eftersträvas med EIT Campus, EIT Digitals plattform för akademiska färdigheter (d)Academy Skills Passport Platform, EIT Deep Tech Talent Initiative (DTTI) och andra relevanta initiativ.   1 Projekt som valts ut inom ramen för ansökningsomgången DIGITAL-2024-ADVANCED-DIGITAL-06-SKILLS.   Tillämpningsområde:  Åtgärden inom detta arbetsområde kommer att syfta till att ytterligare utvidga verksamheten på de nationella koalitionernas webbplatser som inrättades inom ramen för FSE-ansökningsomgångarna 2019 och 2020 och ansökningsomgången för det digitala området 2024, samt stödja inrättandet av nya webbplatser i medlemsstater som ännu inte har någon nationell koalition eller webbplats.  Verksamheten inom det andra arbetsområdet kommer att   Utveckla och koppla samman de nationella koalitionernas infrastrukturer (webbplatser) som ännu inte är anslutna till kärnplattformen genom interoperabla sammanlänkningar som integrerar och möjliggör utbyten med kärnplattformens komponenter.  Ge tillgång till nationella/regionala/lokala aktörer och metoder och bygga interoperabla länkar för att tillhandahålla tjänster som är relevanta för det lokala sammanhanget.  Utöka och engagera nationella koalitioner som redan är anslutna till kärnplattformen.   Stödet till nationella koalitioner i en viss medlemsstat kan ges i form av ekonomiskt stöd till tredje parter (FSTP) på högst 150 000 euro per tredje part för att möjliggöra tillräcklig finansiering för genomförandet av deras verksamhet.

title: Cultură, creativitate și societate favorabilă incluziunii 2026
description: Rezultatul preconizat:  Proiectele ar trebui să contribuie la toate rezultatele preconizate următoare:   Factorii de decizie de la nivelul UE, de la nivel național și local dețin cunoștințele necesare pentru a contribui la elaborarea reglementărilor, standardelor și instrumentelor electorale care abordează utilizarea tehnologiilor digitale în alegeri și în campaniile politice, asigurând integritatea, incluziunea, accesibilitatea, echitatea, transparența și securitatea acestora.  Organizațiile implicate în procesele electorale elaborează și pun în aplicare orientări pentru utilizarea responsabilă a tehnologiilor digitale în alegeri și în campaniile politice, aliniate la reglementările UE și naționale.  Creșterea transparenței și a responsabilității în campaniile politice bazate pe IA, realizată prin cerințe privind auditurile sistemelor de IA, divulgarea datelor, transparența în ceea ce privește algoritmii și sursele modelelor lingvistice de mari dimensiuni (LLM) și dezvoltarea responsabilă a IA.    Domeniul de aplicare:  Integritatea proceselor electorale din Europa se confruntă cu provocări în era digitală. Transformarea digitală a proceselor democratice a creat noi căi de implicare a cetățenilor, dar prezintă, de asemenea, riscuri semnificative, de la dezinformare la integritatea proceselor electorale și a altor procese democratice. Preocupările cu privire la ingerințele externe, exemplificate de activitățile Rusiei, dar și de alte țări terțe, au subliniat necesitatea unor măsuri solide de protejare a proceselor electorale, inclusiv consolidarea securității cibernetice și a verificării alegătorilor pentru a preveni manipularea electorală percepută. Platformele de comunicare socială, în special, au devenit câmpuri de luptă din ce în ce mai critice în lupta pentru opinia publică, instrumentele bazate pe IA fiind utilizate pentru a amplifica și a răspândi în mod artificial dezinformarea, pentru a manipula discursul public și pentru a influența comportamentul alegătorilor.  Pentru a aborda aceste provocări, este esențial să se examineze efectele tehnologiilor digitale asupra opiniei publice și a guvernanței și să se investigheze dezvoltarea IA etice, a publicității politice transparente și a instrumentelor de combatere a dezinformării, a dezinformării și a manipulării informațiilor și a ingerințelor străine (FIMI). Aceasta include explorarea potențialului tehnologiilor digitale de a transforma și de a îmbunătăți procesele democratice, investigarea abordărilor multipartite, acordând o atenție deosebită promovării dialogului cu platformele online, mass-media și partidele și mișcările politice, precum și consolidării mass-mediei tradiționale și a celei noi și asigurării unor platforme alternative pentru a spori reziliența electorală.  Propunerile ar trebui, de asemenea, să investigheze riscurile pe care noile tehnologii le prezintă pentru integritatea democratică, în special prin manipularea opiniei publice și a proceselor electorale, explorând, în același timp, modalități de a valorifica aceste noi tehnologii pentru a înțelege mai bine și a atenua aceste amenințări. Propunerile sunt, de asemenea, încurajate să examineze modul în care conținutul generat de IA în mass-media, inclusiv în mass-media de divertisment, influențează opinia publică, discursurile sociale, stereotipurile și normele de gen și angajamentul civic. În plus, propunerile pot lua în considerare strategii pentru punerea în aplicare a unor măsuri criptografice adecvate, inclusiv investigarea abordărilor bazate pe criptografia postcuantică.  Instituțiile UE s-au implicat activ în abordarea principalelor provocări pentru integritatea alegerilor, inclusiv amplificarea artificială a dezinformării, responsabilitatea platformelor online și protecția proceselor democratice. Propunerile ar trebui să țină seama de inițiativele politice și strategice în curs, în special de Regulamentul privind publicitatea politică, de Regulamentul privind IA, de orientările electorale din Regulamentul privind serviciile digitale  [1]  și de Recomandarea Comisiei din 2023 privind alegeri incluzive și reziliente, precum și de Codul de conduită privind dezinformarea  [2].   Scopul final este de a înțelege cum se pot crea sisteme electorale robuste și reziliente care să poată răspunde provocărilor erei digitale, să asigure siguranța și integritatea proceselor electorale și să promoveze alegeri libere, echitabile, favorabile incluziunii, accesibile și transparente. Acest lucru necesită investigarea riscurilor de atacuri cibernetice și de ingerințe străine asupra proceselor electorale, elaborarea de strategii de consolidare a securității sistemului de vot și de promovare a transparenței alegerilor, dezvoltarea unor sisteme de alertă timpurie, a unor strategii eficace de demascare și a unor măsuri de responsabilizare pentru platforme.  Cercetarea ar trebui să aibă o abordare interdisciplinară (inclusiv disciplinele SSH), reunind o gamă diversă de părți interesate, inclusiv – dar fără a se limita la acestea – autorități electorale și alte autorități naționale cu responsabilități în materie electorală – în special cele reprezentate în Rețeaua europeană de cooperare privind alegerile – organizații ale societății civile, mass-media noi și tradiționale și platforme digitale.  Proiectele se pot axa, de asemenea, pe modul în care FIMI pot influența discursul politic prin intermediul platformelor digitale, în special în perioadele electorale, inclusiv în moduri care subminează drepturile femeilor, ale persoanelor LGBTIQ, ale persoanelor cu handicap și ale altor grupuri subreprezentate. Acest lucru implică, de asemenea, examinarea siguranței proceselor electorale, protejarea integrității alegerilor și menținerea încrederii publice în procesul democratic, cu un accent deosebit pe asigurarea siguranței și securității candidaților politici, în special a femeilor și a persoanelor LGBTIQ și a altor membri ai grupurilor minoritare, împotriva violenței, intimidării și hărțuirii. Abordarea acestor preocupări necesită o înțelegere cuprinzătoare a modului în care IA modelează campaniile politice, discursurile din mass-media, implicarea publicului și răspândirea dezinformării (de gen).  Propunerile sunt încurajate să identifice alte proiecte finanțate de UE legate de integritatea electorală în cadrul programului Orizont Europa (inclusiv, dar fără a se limita la cele din domeniul securității cibernetice și al cercetării și dezvoltării IA) și scheme de finanțare complementare, cum ar fi programul „Cetățeni, egalitate, drepturi și valori” și programul Europa digitală, și să exploreze potențiale oportunități de colaborare cu acestea.  Solicitanții pot lua în considerare participarea Centrului Comun de Cercetare (JRC) pentru a valorifica gama largă de capacități științifice și tehnice ale acestuia, inclusiv expertiza sa în domeniul tehnologiilor digitale, al științei datelor și al securității cibernetice, pentru a sprijini obiectivele proiectelor și a spori impactul general al acestora. title: Civil Security for Society 2027
description: Expected Outcome:  Project results are expected to contribute to  some or all  of the following expected outcomes:   Development, testing and integration of issuance, validation and sharing capabilities for possible future types (beyond Type 1) of Digital Travel Credentials (DTC);  Integration of innovative, on-the-move, biometrics and remote biometric acquisition modalities to support the use of DTCs;  Improved secure connectivity and interoperability for future DTCs;  Improved capability of issuance of emergency travel documents and/or emergency DTCs.    Scope:  Issuance, verification and management of digital travel credentials (DTCs) is relevant for border management, immigration and visa management. Furthermore, it could also be relevant to combat illicit activities such as terrorism, crime or frauds. This topic aims at supporting research and innovation that explore, develop and test enhanced capabilities for securely issuing, verify and manage (including sharing) possible future types of digital travel credentials (DTCs) for travel across the external borders of the EU.  The proposed solutions must be compatible with current, planned or foreseeable EU DTCs formats, and with applicable International Civil Aviation Organisation (ICAO) schemes, but they should also push forward to possible further types of DTCs (“Type 2” and “Type 3”).  Additionally, the funded actions should also work on the integration of current and new biometrics, and/or new biometric acquisition modality, in support of DTCs. This includes but does not limit to biometrics such as fingermark, palmprint, palmmark, rolled fingerprint, contactless fingerphotos, and biometric acquisition modalities such as remote and on-the-move, including those modalities developed by previous projects funded by this Destination of Horizon Europe Cluster 3. The project should develop and/or contribute to reference biometric sample quality assessments standards for these biometric modalities included in the DTCs, compatibly with existing relevant tools such as the Open Source Face Image Quality (OFIQ), or improving forward-looking interoperability, for example between contact and contactless fingerprint data.  The funded research project(s) can also address the use case of verification, issuance or re-issuance of (emergency) DTCs in cases of emergencies (including evacuations of EU citizens).  Funded research can additionally address the security of breeder documents, which risk to be “weak links” when they are used to obtain genuine, secure travel credentials.  Proposals submitted under this topic are expected to address the priorities of the European Border and Coast Guard and of its Agency (Frontex) and of the European Union Agency for the Operational Management of Large-Scale IT Systems in the Area of Freedom, Security and Justice (eu-LISA). This should start from the definition of requirements and the design phase of their work, including basing on the EBCG Capability Roadmap; and on the engagement with the Agencies during the implementation of the project. At the stage of proposal preparation, Frontex and eu-LISA will not provide any guidance on, or otherwise be involved in the preparation of, project proposals. Proposals should consider and foresee that Frontex and eu-LISA may observe pilots and demonstrations when the project will be implemented, with the aim of facilitating future uptake of innovations for the border and coast guard community.  To ensure the active involvement of and timely feedback from relevant security practitioners, proposals should plan a mid-term deliverable consisting in the assessment of the project’s mid-term outcomes, performed by the practitioners involved in the project.  null   Activities are expected to achieve TRL 4-5 by the end of the project – see General Annex B.

description: Expected Outcome:  The topic encompasses actions within the scope of the co-programmed European Partnership on Globally Competitive Space Systems (‘Space Partnership’) in the areas of satellite communication (SatCom), Earth Observation (EO) and New Commercial Space Transportation Solutions and is part of cohesive activities in the domain of digital developments under the grand heading of “digitalisation for commercial space solutions”.  Under the area of  Access to Space  related to New Space Transportation Solutions, this topic focusses on the  maturation of disruptive/game changing digital technologies [1]   required to strengthen competitiveness in this domain.  Project results are expected to contribute to one or several of the following expected outcomes:   Improved space transportation systems and launcher sustainability, reduced costs and operational constraints as well as enhanced system monitoring and autonomy;  Innovative technologies for New Space Transportation Solutions, including addressing software and digital tools.     This will contribute to developing, deploying global space-based services applications and data and contribute to fostering the EU's space sector competitiveness and sustainability, as stated in the expected impact of this destination.  Scope:  To tackle the above-mentioned expected outcomes, R&I is expected to address the maturation of disruptive/game changing digital technologies required to strengthen competitiveness in this domain and sustainability by assessing the impact of these technologies (e.g. by allowing the monitoring of sustainable solutions). More specifically, R&I in one or more of the following areas are expected to be addressed:    Autonomy, data fusion, navigation, mission planning, and more specifically advanced algorithms for process automation and autonomous flight termination systems;   Eco-design guidelines for end-to-end aspects and software design tools, and more specifically digital models of the launch system through the use of Model-Based System Engineering, and modelling/simulation of space activity impact on atmosphere;   Landing solutions for reusability, specifically navigation data fusion for autonomous landing.    Proposals are expected to promote cooperation between different actors (industry, SMEs, research institutions and academia) and consider opportunities to quickly turn technological innovation into commercial use in space.  It is expected that projects make use of existing EU technologies and/or building blocks, including at component level, contributing to EU non-dependence and strengthening competitiveness, and this should be clearly presented in the proposal. Furthermore, proposed activities should be complementary to H2020 and Horizon Europe funded projects, national activities and activities funded by the European Space Agency (ESA).  This topic contributes to the implementation of the co-programmed European Partnership on ‘Globally Competitive Space Systems’ (GCSS).   In this topic, the integration of the gender dimension (sex and gender analysis) in research and innovation content should be addressed only if relevant in relation to the objectives of the research effort.  null   Activities are expected to achieve TRL 7-8 by the end of the project. The reference TRL definition is the ISO 16290:2013 applicable to the space sector.    [1] Identified in the Strategic Research and Innovation Agenda (SRIA) of the co-Programmed European Partnership on Globally Competitive Space Systems (https://www.space-aisbl.org/sria/)

title: Acțiuni de dezvoltare puse în aplicare prin granturi pentru costuri reale
description: Domeniul de aplicare:  Reducerea barierelor administrative rămâne o provocare pentru deplasarea rapidă a forțelor armate dincolo de frontierele statelor membre ale UE și ale țărilor asociate FED, în special într-un mediu geopolitic în continuă deteriorare. Digitalizarea peisajului permisului de mobilitate militară și al autorizării este, prin urmare, esențială pentru desfășurări rapide și eficiente.  În acest context, acest subiect urmărește să monitorizeze și să completeze activitățile din acest domeniu cu obiectivul de a dezvolta un sistem rezilient, inclusiv cu o aplicație mobilă, capabil să funcționeze în condiții nefavorabile atunci când nu sunt disponibile toate nodurile sistemului. Acest lucru va necesita punerea în aplicare a unor metode avansate de criptare pentru a proteja schimburile de informații sensibile și urgente, precum și capacități integrate de urmărire și monitorizare.  Acest subiect contribuie la obiectivele STEP, astfel cum sunt definite în Regulamentul STEP, în domeniul-țintă de investiții al tehnologiilor de apărare.   Tipuri specifice de activități:  Studii, proiectare, creare de prototipuri, testare, calificare și certificare, fără a exclude activitățile din amonte și din aval eligibile pentru acțiuni de dezvoltare.   Buget orientativ:  9 000 000 EUR pentru acest subiect în cadrul cererii de propuneri FED-2026-AD.   Numărul orientativ de propuneri care urmează să fie finanțate:  O propunere urmează să fie finanțată pentru acest subiect. Cu toate acestea, în funcție de calitatea propunerilor prezentate și de bugetul disponibil, în cele din urmă pot fi finanțate mai multe propuneri pentru acest subiect.

title: HORIZON-JU-Chips-2026-3-RIA
description: Resultado esperado:  La atención debe centrarse en los ámbitos en los que los países de la Asociación Digital aportan una sólida experiencia complementaria, incluidos los envases avanzados, la integración heterogénea y las tecnologías de chips fotónicos. El tema tendría por objeto fomentar la colaboración entre las comunidades de I+i de los países de la Asociación Europea y Digital. Se espera que los proyectos contribuyan a los siguientes resultados:  • Conceptos innovadores de diseño e integración para sistemas informáticos neuromórficos que soportan un consumo de energía muy bajo, conectividad y funciones integradas para aplicaciones móviles.  • Tecnologías de proceso de fabricación alternativas para chips semiconductores incluyendo frontend o backend para integración heterogénea. Las tecnologías deben sostener a medio y largo plazo la rápida evolución del rendimiento, la miniaturización y el coste de los dispositivos, reduciendo al mismo tiempo la huella ambiental.  • Soluciones de envasado muy avanzadas destinadas a la integración heterogénea de múltiples funciones y materiales para aplicaciones en comunicación (RF, mmW o THz), detección, accionamiento, gestión de potencia e integración activa/pasiva.

description: Expected Outcome:      European leadership in foresight activities on future enabling technologies and their transformational potential in industrial, societal and environmental terms.  Increased collaboration between academia, industry players and other relevant stakeholders in iterative and multidisciplinary approaches for co-creating the enabling technologies of the future.  Alignment with national or regional initiatives creating an expanding innovation ecosystem, anchored in local contexts across Europe, for selected emerging technologies.  Accelerating the pick-up of novel advanced technology by industry and society.    Scope:  Proposals should establish a forum for emerging interdisciplinary areas and new technological visions.  Proposals should enable and support a broad range of participants (across disciplines in science and engineering, RTOs, industry sectors, stakeholders) to meet, mutually inspire, cooperate and develop together innovative ideas for future enabling digital technologies covering from fundamental research up to proof of concept.  Proposals should involve and be driven by representatives of the relevant actors of the field (e.g., academia, RTOs, industry including SMEs).  Proposals should consider civil society engagement for seeking wider input.  Proposals should connect with analogous EC-internal activities, either ongoing (e.g. FOSI4EIC involving EISMEA and JRC) or foreseen, such as the Competitiveness Coordination Tool and the technology observatory envisaged in the FP10 regulation.  Beneficiaries that intend to transfer ownership or grant an exclusive licence must formally notify the granting authority (i.e. DG-CNECT and HaDEA) before the intended transfer or licensing takes place and the granting authority may up to four years after the end of the action object to a transfer of ownership or the exclusive licensing of results.

description: Expected Outcome:  Proposals are expected to contribute one or more of the following:   Practical robust implementations of PQC schemes that can withstand implementation attacks including side-channel attacks, fault attacks and combined attacks, and design of automated tools for evaluating the security of PQC implementations. Comprehensive guidelines for implementing countermeasures against a wide range of attacks;  Advances in understanding the quantum hardness of mathematical problem classes; new quantum algorithms and improvements in quantum programming and implementation; security validation methods; design of post-quantum schemes with improved security against quantum and AI-based attacks;  Post-quantum schemes and protocols to support privacy-friendly applications and services, ncluding the secure and private use of electronic identities. Design of new digital signatures, key encapsulation mechanisms, and other schemes or use of existing ones to build new verification protocols.    Scope:  Securing PQC algorithm implementations is vital to protect against implementation attacks, such as side channel attacks, fault attacks and combinations of these, which may be amplified by deep learning. Current countermeasures incur significant overhead, and new approaches are needed to balance security and performance. Formal verification tools and methodologies can help achieve this goal and provide machine-readable evidence. Furthermore, to boost confidence in PQC systems, their security should be assessed, including the potential impact of new quantum algorithms or new optimizations of existing ones, also combined with AI.  Another key research area is digital trust in the post-quantum era, which requires transforming various areas, such as secure identities, data protection, access to essential services, and applications such as backup recovery, browser extensions and others into trusted and reliable solutions, via new post-quantum schemes and advanced building blocks for privacy-enhancing protocols.  Proposals should address one of the following technology areas:   Development of solutions to prevent implementation attacks, balancing security, performance and cost; research in new attacks, including AI-powered ones, and/or combination of attacks, to inform secure design; creation of testing frameworks for automated security evaluations; improvement of formal verification methodologies.  Quantum hardness analysis, via the study of the impact of new quantum algorithms or improvement of existing quantum algorithm implementations as well as the impact of AI-supported quantum attacks; analysis of cryptanalysis results; design of new post-quantum schemes using the information of the advances achieved/ fine-tuning of parameters sets.  Design of quantum-resistant schemes and protocols supporting the field of privacy-friendly applications and services, including electronic identities, verification protocols and pseudonymous access options, protocols for attestation and anonymous attestation, for real world scenarios, via the design of new digital signature schemes and key encapsulation mechanisms, design of advanced cryptographic schemes, and usage of existing schemes in new protocols, for post-quantum digital identity and digital trust systems.

title: DIGITAL
description: Expected Outcome:  Proposals are expected to contribute to the following outcomes:   Increasing the participation and influence of European experts in digital standardisation to promote EU values and strategic interests, contributing to strengthen EU competitiveness in the digital field.  Improvement of the skills of European experts, especially from SMEs, R&I institutions, Open-Source community, academia and societal stakeholders, to successfully contribute and lead in the development of digital standards.  Development and update of standardisation landscapes and gap analyses of key digital technologies as outlined in the Rolling Plan for ICT Standardisation.  Provision of foresight analyses regarding standardisation in new emerging technologies to identify short and medium-term digital standardisation needs to support EU policies and anticipate appropriate participation by EU stakeholders.  More awareness of the benefits and competitive advantages of standardisation, in particular for SMEs and researchers, and more visibility of the European digital standardisation ecosystem.    Scope:  Contribute to the implementation of the EU Standardisation Strategy and other policy initiatives such as Europe’s Digital Decade, Apply AI Strategy or the Competitiveness Compass, with an emphasis on supporting the EU’s leading position in global standards-setting of key digital technologies.  The goals are inter alia to 1) strengthen the EU competitiveness in the digital domain; 2) contribute to EU tech sovereignty and 3) promote EU values and interests internationally, by empowering and financially supporting the active participation of European stakeholders in the development of digital international standards.  The objective is to reinforce the presence of experts from the EU and associated Horizon Europe countries in global digital standards setting, especially those coming from SMEs, R&I institutions, Open-Source community, academia and societal stakeholders.  To achieve this objective, proposals under this topic should provide for:   Setting up of a management facility to support contributions and leadership (e.g. chairing of technical committees, convenor positions) of European specialists in activities in relation to global digital standardisation  When relevant, support financially the hosting of international standardisation meetings (e.g. 3GPP, ISO/IEC JTC1) and workshops in Europe to ease the participation of European experts  Landscape and gap analysis of standardisation activities in key digital priority areas, as outlined in the Annual Union Work Programme and the Rolling Plan for ICT standardisation, including identification of new emerging technology areas.  Promotion of the relevance and benefits of digital standardisation, especially for strengthening the competitiveness of EU industry, driving sustainability, achieving tech sovereignty, and promoting EU values. The proposal shall build synergies with other similar EU- and national-funded initiatives. It shall also include actions, including development of tools and materials, to promote education and skills on standardisation.    Beneficiaries that intend to transfer ownership or grant an exclusive licence must formally notify the granting authority (i.e. DG-CNECT and HaDEA) before the intended transfer or licensing takes place and the granting authority may up to four years after the end of the action object to a transfer of ownership or the exclusive licensing of results.  The proposal should take into account the previous activities carried out at least in terms of educational material and facilities for funding experts within the topics ICT-40-2017 (implemented by the StandICT.eu project), ICT-45-2020 (implemented under StandICT.eu2023 project), HORIZON-CL4-2022-RESILIENCE-01-21 (implemented under StandICT.eu 2026) and HORIZON-CL4-2024-HUMAN-03-04 (implemented under StandICT.eu 2029). title: Apoyar la implementación de la Misión Restaurar nuestro Océano y Aguas
description: Resultado esperado:  Se espera que los resultados del proyecto contribuyan a todos los siguientes resultados esperados:   Se ponen a disposición activos regionales y locales adicionales (datos, modelos, gemelos digitales) en la infraestructura básica de la DTO, EDITO;  Nuevas aplicaciones digitales gemelas, haciendo hincapié en las condiciones regionales y locales y abordando las consideraciones regionales, incluidas las necesidades de las partes interesadas, la disponibilidad de datos, etc.;  mejora de las capacidades regionales digitales gemelas, creando en la UE la infraestructura básica de la DTO, la EDITO, las condiciones para apoyar directamente la aplicación de las políticas, incluida la política de medio ambiente marino, y las aplicaciones de la economía azul que se basan en las características regionales de la cuenca marítima;  Desarrollo de bibliotecas regionales de hipótesis hipotéticas, incluidos umbrales de confianza y análisis conexos, cuantificación de las condiciones necesarias para aumentar los niveles de confianza, etc.;  Apoyo al seguimiento y la gestión sostenible de los mares regionales con nuevos servicios adaptados a los mares regionales.    Ámbito de aplicación:  Las propuestas deben establecer componentes regionales dentro de la infraestructura básica de EDITO del gemelo digital del océano de la UE. Estos componentes regionales deben fomentar el desarrollo de aplicaciones de gemelos digitales locales: herramientas digitales personalizadas diseñadas para abordar las prioridades únicas de comunidades locales de partes interesadas específicas.  Para cada cuenca marítima (un proyecto por faro), el objetivo es:   Identificar, agregar e integrar los datos regionales existentes (a través de EMODnet), las herramientas, la modelización y los activos gemelos digitales locales que aún no son ampliamente públicos (incluidos los activos de aguas interiores que son pertinentes para el enfoque integrado de fuente a mar, haciendo hincapié en las conexiones tierra-mar  [1])  y adoptar las medidas necesarias para ponerlos a disposición a través de EDITO, siguiendo todos los protocolos de interoperabilidad y normalización necesarios. Los tipos de datos infrarrepresentados (biologaje, telemetría acústica, etc.) revisten especial interés;  Desarrollar servicios gemelos digitales regionales (aplicaciones y servicios adaptados que aborden los retos específicos de cada región, incluidos, por ejemplo, los retos de las pequeñas islas, la resiliencia costera, la conservación y restauración de la biodiversidad, la contaminación, la adaptación al cambio climático, la pesca y la acuicultura y otros sectores de la economía azul). Estos servicios deben centrarse tanto en cuestiones relevantes para las políticas como en cuestiones relacionadas con el desarrollo de una economía azul regional sostenible y competitiva. Para apoyar las capacidades predictivas, la doble evolución digital regional debe buscar, en particular, la integración de conjuntos de datos de seguimiento ecológico y de biodiversidad a largo plazo, garantizando que la modelización y las hipótesis se basen en observaciones empíricas de series temporales;  Fomentar la participación de las partes interesadas regionales (autoridades regionales, convenios marítimos regionales, socios de la industria y comunidades locales) para incorporar los activos existentes (bases de datos, modelos locales o regionales) para el diseño conjunto y la validación de aplicaciones digitales gemelas para la elaboración de políticas eficaces y el apoyo a las decisiones operativas;  Mejorar la adopción intensiva de algoritmos innovadores de inteligencia artificial y gestión de macrodatos.  A través del compromiso antes mencionado, y a través de procesos de co-creación, desarrollar una gama de escenarios hipotéticos, evaluar sus niveles de confianza e identificar acciones hacia la mejora de dicha confianza.    [1]    En el caso de los activos identificados en la IDEACIÓN CSA y financiados en el marco de «HORIZON-MISS-2023-OCEAN-01-09 hacia la integración de las aguas interiores en el océano gemelo digital». https://cordis.europa.eu/project/id/101157371

description: Resultado esperado:  Los proyectos deben contribuir a todos los siguientes resultados esperados:   Las instituciones de la UE y los responsables nacionales de la toma de decisiones tienen una mejor comprensión de cómo fomentar la resiliencia democrática a través de la alfabetización mediática y digital, equipando a las sociedades para adaptarse y prosperar frente a la evolución de los desafíos tecnológicos, políticos y sociales.  Los ciudadanos están facultados para navegar por el panorama digital con discernimiento y pensamiento crítico, participando activamente con los medios de comunicación y otras fuentes de información, garantizando una participación democrática informada.    Ámbito de aplicación:  Como se recuerda en el informe «Safer together» [1],  «en los últimos años, la Comisión ya ha tomado medidas para luchar contra las amenazas híbridas (incluida la manipulación de información e injerencia extranjeras/IFMI) y mejorar la resiliencia democrática en toda la UE. Adoptó, entre otras iniciativas, el Plan de Acción para la Democracia Europea  [2]  para construir democracias más resilientes en toda la UE mediante la promoción de elecciones libres y justas, el refuerzo de la libertad de los medios de comunicación, la lucha contra la desinformación y la manipulación de información e injerencia por parte de agentes extranjeros y la promoción de la integridad de la información. Con la adopción de la Ley de Servicios Digitales  [3]  y sus obligaciones vinculantes para las plataformas en línea de luchar contra la difusión de desinformación, la Comisión también reforzó el Código de Buenas Prácticas en materia de Desinformación, que se convirtió en un Código de Conducta en el marco de la Ley de Servicios Digitales. Además, la puesta en marcha del Observatorio Europeo de los Medios de Comunicación Digitales (EDMO) y sus centros aumentaron la capacidad de detectar, analizar y exponer campañas de desinformación». [4]   La Estrategia de la Unión de Preparación  [5]  subraya que la preparación es una responsabilidad colectiva. También señala la necesidad de aumentar la resiliencia de nuestras democracias, en particular con vistas a reforzar la confianza en las instituciones, que puede ser crucial en situaciones de crisis, como se ha visto, por ejemplo, durante la pandemia de COVID-19. Los grupos que se encuentran en una situación vulnerable en particular, como los niños, las personas mayores y las personas con discapacidad, las minorías étnicas o religiosas, las personas LGBTIQ, las personas que sufren pobreza o exclusión social, se ven afectados de manera desproporcionada por las crisis, lo que a menudo exacerba las desventajas, barreras y desigualdades preexistentes.  La desinformación es especialmente perjudicial, ya que socava la confianza pública y puede exacerbar el impacto de las crisis. Los ciudadanos comprometidos, informados y empoderados son la mejor garantía para la resiliencia de nuestras democracias. Las autoridades públicas, las escuelas, las universidades y las instituciones de formación, las iniciativas juveniles, las organizaciones y asociaciones de la sociedad civil, los interlocutores sociales, las empresas, las redes y comunidades locales y los ciudadanos desde una edad temprana desempeñan un papel vital en este esfuerzo colectivo, y la investigación propuesta debe adoptar un enfoque multiactor.  En este contexto, la investigación propuesta debe explorar los patrones complejos y dinámicos de los comportamientos de los usuarios en la era digital, investigando cómo las personas buscan, evalúan e interactúan con la información en línea y fuera de línea. Tal exploración se beneficiará de incluir un análisis de la dinámica emocional en la difusión de desinformación y polarización en plataformas digitales. Esto es especialmente relevante en contextos de crisis en los que la manipulación de la información y la desinformación extranjeras pueden aprovecharse para aumentar el pánico y la confusión. Las propuestas deben investigar cómo los algoritmos amplifican el contenido emotivo, fomentando la polarización y socavando la confianza en las instituciones democráticas, así como la respuesta a las crisis y desarrollar estrategias digitales y de alfabetización mediática para contrarrestar narrativas emocionalmente manipuladoras, como los discursos populistas y posteriores a la verdad.  La investigación también debe examinar los factores que influyen en la alfabetización digital, los hábitos de búsqueda de información y el compromiso en línea, centrándose en mejorar la participación y el compromiso de los ciudadanos a través de medios digitales (también a través de la tecnología cívica) y la toma de decisiones informada. En un momento en que la desinformación se utiliza para sembrar la discordia explotando los temores de los ciudadanos, es crucial garantizar que las decisiones democráticas se basen en los hechos y las fuentes de información disponibles más fiables y ampliamente aceptados. La investigación debe explorar el papel fundamental que puede desempeñar la alfabetización digital y mediática en el fomento de la resiliencia social y la integridad de la información, permitiendo a los ciudadanos navegar y resistir la desinformación y la desinformación.  Las propuestas deben planificar una evaluación crítica de las iniciativas de alfabetización mediática y digital  [6]  para evaluar si los esfuerzos existentes están mejorando la resiliencia de los ciudadanos o si se necesitan nuevos enfoques para equipar más eficazmente a los ciudadanos contra la evolución de las tácticas de manipulación.  La investigación debe identificar estrategias para mejorar la alfabetización mediática y la alfabetización digital y mediática, con el fin de mejorar el pensamiento crítico, promover la toma de decisiones basada en pruebas y contrarrestar los efectos negativos de la desinformación en las sociedades democráticas. Para facilitar la generación de soluciones prácticas para educadores y responsables políticos, la investigación podría utilizar herramientas computacionales, como el análisis de redes sociales y el procesamiento del lenguaje natural, para mapear y mitigar la difusión de desinformación en múltiples plataformas. Esto incluye identificar el Comportamiento Inauthentic Coordinado y analizar el contenido textual y visual para informar las iniciativas de alfabetización mediática.  Se anima a las propuestas a identificar otros proyectos pertinentes financiados por la UE relacionados con la alfabetización mediática y digital, y a explorar posibles oportunidades de colaboración con ellos. Se recomienda encarecidamente la agrupación y la cooperación con otros proyectos seleccionados en relación con este tema y otros proyectos pertinentes.  Se anima a los proyectos seleccionados para su financiación a que colaboren con el CCI para buscar sinergias con su trabajo en materia de innovación para la democracia y la gobernanza pública. description: Expected Outcome:  Project results are expected to contribute to  some or all  of the following expected outcomes:   Developed a tailored education programs for younger generations, incorporating digital tools and gamification to enhance disaster awareness and engagement;  Strengthened societal resilience by actively involving younger generations, citizens, and local authorities in disaster preparedness and response initiatives;  Promoted collaborative research that integrates youth perspectives and community involvement, fostering a more resilient society in the face of disasters and crises;  Enhanced resilience and behaviour of children, young people, and other groups in a vulnerable situation before, during, and after climate-related disasters and health emergencies;  Training and education tools to engage young people and other populations a vulnerable situation in preparedness and crisis management.    Scope:  This topic focuses on enhancing societal resilience by actively engaging younger generations in disaster preparedness, response, and recovery through digital innovation, education, and community involvement. Projects should develop tailored innovative solutions that integrate digital tools, gamification, and interactive learning methods to improve disaster awareness, risk perception, and response capabilities among younger generations. These initiatives should empower younger generations [1] , to become active contributors to resilience-building efforts, equipping them with the knowledge and leadership skills.  Particular attention should be given to the behaviour of children, young people, and other groups in a vulnerable situation before, during, and after climate-related disasters and health emergencies. Participatory approaches, including youth-led initiatives, citizen science, and digital engagement platforms, should be prioritized to enhance community-based resilience and ensure young people’s perspectives are integrated into decision-making processes. These approaches should follow an intersectional approach that gives credit to the (growing) heterogeneity of young people. Best practices from other programmes should be taken into account.  Proposals should also focus on leveraging emerging technologies - such as artificial intelligence, virtual and augmented reality, social media analytics, and serious games - to engage young people in disaster preparedness and crisis response. Additionally, innovative communication strategies should be explored to enhance youth participation, particularly through digital technologies and social media. Practical examples, including pilots and real-world case studies, should be developed to test and refine these approaches.  Proposals should explore methods to interconnect young people’s data with crisis management teams, practitioners, and authorities, ensuring that their contributions are effectively integrated into emergency response frameworks. Training and education tools should be designed to engage young people and other vulnerable populations in preparedness and crisis management, promoting long-term resilience.  Projects should conduct a stakeholder or market analysis and a roadmap or plan for uptake of the developed methodologies, findings, and technologies to the industry, the research and innovation community, and/or the relevant authorities.  The support and involvement of citizens and civil society is central to achieving the targeted outcomes.  By fostering collaborative research and youth-driven initiatives, projects should contribute to innovative and inclusive resilience strategies that align with EU policies on disaster risk reduction, education, digital transformation, and civil protection. Proposals should ensure synergies with existing initiatives and frameworks, such as the Preparedness Union Strategy’s chapter on population preparedness, Erasmus+ and the European Solidarity Corps, as well as the Sendai Disaster Risk Reduction Framework. Finding synergies with projects from operational grants, such as the Knowledge for Action in Prevention & Preparedness (KAPP) [2] , is recommend.  null   Activities are expected to achieve TRL 5 by the end of the project – see General Annex B.   [1] In the context of the European Union, youth is typically defined as individuals between the ages of 13 and 30. This definition aligns with the EU's Youth Strategy, which focuses on supporting young people’s personal and professional development. However, some EU programs may adjust the age range slightly depending on the specific context (e.g., education, employment, or participation), but the 13-30 age bracket is recognized in EU policies related to youth. title: Acções de apoio ao programa
description: Resultado esperado:   Otimização do quadro operacional de D&E para o Programa Europa Digital, tendo em conta os elementos mencionados no âmbito de aplicação, com abordagens metodológicas e práticas sólidas.  Identificação de diferentes tipos de adotantes e criação de uma taxonomia que articule os respetivos interesses e necessidades.  Apoio a projetos na preparação e execução de atividades de D&E, incluindo a valorização e a adoção dos resultados através de serviços de aconselhamento, apoio às empresas e aceleração  Um plano para concretizar o quadro operacional apoiado por métricas de acompanhamento e avaliação.  A realização de ações de execução do quadro operacional e a participação das partes interessadas, se for caso disso, incluindo eventos setoriais e a nível do programa.  Os meios e instrumentos para facilitar a execução do quadro operacional, incluindo os requisitos funcionais e técnicos para uma plataforma de resultados específica.  Um plano para a sustentabilidade do quadro operacional e das ações executadas pelo projeto.  Difusão e exploração dos resultados (incluindo o acesso às infraestruturas) no contexto específico das restrições de segurança e da proteção dos interesses da UE em geral.  Produzir uma base de dados com casos concretos de resultados do PED, em todos os objetivos específicos e organismos de execução, com divulgação e utilização exemplares dos resultados.   Objectivo:  Maximizar o impacto do Programa Europa Digital e a adoção dos seus resultados através de um quadro operacional de divulgação e exploração (D&E) e da execução de ações práticas apoiadas por instrumentos adequados. A ação impulsionará os esforços de D&E já em curso a nível do programa e reforçá-los-á.  O Programa Europa Digital procura melhorar a valorização dos resultados dos projetos e a sua adoção efetiva. Espera-se, por conseguinte, que as atividades de divulgação e exploração (D&E) contribuam substancialmente para a realização dos objetivos do programa.  As ações financiadas pelo programa devem executar atividades de difusão e exploração eficientes e direcionadas, a fim de aumentar o impacto do financiamento da UE. Para além dos trabalhos D&E de projetos individuais, o programa financia atividades de apoio em determinados domínios temáticos que apoiam os projetos na respetiva área.  Além disso, existe uma clara necessidade de uma perspetiva global do programa em matéria de D&E. Uma ação de coordenação e apoio em curso (DEDEP.eu)   está a conceber um quadro conceptual e operacional para a execução de atividades eficazes de D&E no programa, ajudando os projetos financiados a partilhar estrategicamente os resultados com as partes interessadas pertinentes e a criar um corpus de materiais e ferramentas reutilizáveis.  O programa está agora a entrar numa fase crucial em que muitas iniciativas estão a produzir resultados tangíveis. Colocar uma forte ênfase na divulgação e exploração destes resultados assegurará uma maior aceitação dos resultados existentes e futuros e amplificará significativamente o impacto global do programa.  Âmbito de aplicação:  A ação abordará, pelo menos, as seguintes dimensões:   O programa global, os seus Objetivos Específicos (OE) e as respetivas áreas, até tópicos e projetos, se for caso disso, em todos os instrumentos de financiamento, em especial subvenções, contratos públicos e instrumentos financeiros;  As vertentes de reforço das capacidades e utilização do Programa Europa Digital, tendo em conta o tipo de resultados e o seu público de divulgação e exploração;  Os diferentes tipos de organizações que participam no programa;  As diferentes partes interessadas, incluindo os utilizadores finais e/ou os utilizadores dos resultados;  As fases do ciclo de vida do projeto e as obrigações de comunicação de informações;  As especificidades de segurança e autonomia estratégica do programa, incluindo as implicações na utilização de infraestruturas críticas e na exploração dos resultados;  coordenação dentro e fora da UE, se for caso disso, tendo em conta as prioridades e iniciativas políticas;  no âmbito do próprio Programa Europa Digital, identificar e explorar complementaridades de projetos entre OE e temas, incluindo ações específicas de coordenação e apoio a OE e agregadores de projetos;  entre o Programa Europa Digital, outros programas da UE e programas nacionais/regionais;  dos diferentes organismos de execução do programa, por exemplo, a Comissão Europeia, a Agência de Execução para a Saúde e o Digital (HADEA), as empresas comuns (EC) e organismos semelhantes, tendo em conta as suas especificidades no tratamento dos resultados resultantes das suas ações. A ação complementará e enriquecerá as atividades de D&E dos projetos do programa. A ação proporcionará meios que podem ajudar a alcançar o seu objetivo, incluindo a mobilização de instrumentos já existentes, por exemplo de outros programas da UE, e a utilização de abordagens inovadoras em matéria de D&E. A ação promoverá a adoção dos resultados do Programa Europa Digital para além das entidades diretamente envolvidas nos projetos do programa.

title: AI Continent
description: Expected Impact:  The objective is to deliver three to four projects that demonstrate the streamlining of regulatory reporting through automated and trusted sharing of compliance data. Each project will address the governance, technical, legal, and processing aspects of the solution.   Objective:    Specific Objective 2 of the Digital Europe Programme aims to reinforce the EU’s core Artificial Intelligence (AI) capacities as a crucial driver for the digital transformation of the public and private sectors.   The vision is to make Europe an AI continent, thriving on the development, integration and adoption of AI. As one of the financial instruments of the upcoming Apply AI Strategy, SO2 will support the development of world class AI models in the EU and foster the integration of AI technologies into EU’s most strategic sectors, including healthcare, energy and research. It will stimulate new industrial uses of AI and improve the delivery of various public services.   In addition, it will support the deployment of new digital solutions for regulatory compliance through data. The objective is to reduce the administrative burden of enterprises by applying advanced digital technologies to automatise the reporting process.     Objectives    This objective will support projects testing digital solutions for transmitting information relevant for compliance with EU legislation (e.g. regulations on environmental issues) and automate the compliance process for  a number of pilot  use cases. These projects will target regulatory reporting requirements, from aggregate data (e.g., company balance sheets) to detailed data (e.g., transactions, events, and product registrations). The aim is to leverage advanced technologies, including data capturing technologies, automatic transmission, analysis, cloud storage, and encryption, to ensure data security, confidentiality, and regulatory compliance. The strong focus should be given to privacy-preserving technologies to ensure trust between the reporting entity and regulatory authorities, safeguarding data confidentiality while enabling secure and efficient compliance processes.   Additionally, the projects will identify burdensome administrative challenges in the selected sectors that could be addressed by automated data-driven solutions, while close collaboration with reporting entities will be essential to enable direct communication with regulatory agencies for automated updates and ensure compliance with evolving regulations. The approach will prioritize access controls and audit trails to enhance transparency and reduce the risk of non-compliance and penalties. Furthermore, the projects could incorporate the European Digital Identity Wallet, when available, to securely identify individuals and legal entities in data spaces, alongside trust services like electronic seals and ledgers.   Scope:     The activities funded under this initiative will focus on the following aspects:    Technical aspects:     Utilize advanced technologies such as privacy-preserving technologies, data capturing technologies, automatic transmission and analysis, cloud storage and encryption for data security and compliance with regulations.     Implement comprehensive APIs to enable real-time compliance and self-compliance checks.     Employ machine learning algorithms for automated monitoring and reporting.     Where possible ,  use precisely defined concepts available in the data catalogue entries of Common European Data Spaces enabling deterministic data collection.     Establish direct communication channels with regulatory authorities for automated updates and reporting, keeping the system updated with changing regulations (e.g. by expressing the reporting requirements in machine readable and executable way).         Ensure robust access control and maintain audit trails for transparency and accountability.            Minimize the risk of non-compliance and potential penalties through these technological and procedural safeguards.            Integrate the European Digital Identity Wallet for secure identification of individuals and legal entities, when available.            Collaborate with providers of data space services and technology, with a particular emphasis on open-source solutions, such as the European Commission's Simpl programme.            All systems must incorporate robust data privacy and security measures.            Proposers must ensure that the systems developed are open source, interoperable with existing government data systems and adhere to European data standards and specifications.            The system must be scalable to handle large volumes of data and high transaction rates.            The system must be designed with end-users in mind, ensuring ease of use and accessibility.            A comprehensive data governance framework must be established. This should include policies for data quality management, data stewardship, and data lifecycle management.            Proposals should target legislations that have clear, quantifiable compliance metrics that can be automatically assessed using data analytics and they should ensure no overlaps with ongoing initiatives (e.g. Digital Product Passport, Customs reform).            This call aims to explore sectors with significant administrative burden such as agriculture, environment, manufacturing, healthcare and energy.

description: Expected Outcome:  Project results are expected to contribute to all of the following expected outcomes:   farmers have increased access to digital tools and advice to improve their resilience to water and nutrient scarcity;  farmers are better prepared for the Green Transition and EU’s new plan for sustainable prosperity and competitiveness;  biodiversity benefits from decreasing water, air and soil pollution while European dependency on mineral fertilisers is reduced.     Scope:  A key challenge for the agricultural sector is to provide food in a context of increasing global population, climate change and price volatility while reducing pollution and preserving natural resources and biodiversity for future generations. Farmers should be able to adopt innovative solutions to increase the resilience to water and to nutrient scarcity. Digital and data technologies offer solutions to monitor parameters (e.g. soil conditions, water and air quality, nutrients content and availability) in a cost-efficient manner while supporting decision-making on input management, adapt to climate change, contribute to cleaner air and biodiversity.  Proposals should:   improve knowledge on the complex interactions between plant, soil, water, air and nutrients (Nitrogen, Phosphorus) in view of climate change in the EU and its impacts on crop production, farming systems (including crop protection use) and the environment, in a representative number of different pedoclimatic regions;  develop and test monitoring devices and systems that can take into account the findings on the interactions described in the previous point, considering their easy integration into other farm management information systems (FMIS) or decision support systems (DSS), and the affordability and accessibility to farmers (such as low connectivity in certain rural areas, digital knowledge, health impairments/disability, etc.);  develop and test AI-enabled decision support systems to better monitor and assess the effects of agricultural practices and land management measures in terms of water and nutrient use taking into account different pedoclimatic zones, local conditions and farm characteristics, their impact on pollution (water, soil) and benefits for biodiversity;  create sets of high-quality AI training data to support the development of DSS with the objective to improve water and nutrient resilience of different farming systems, and make them publicly available, considering legal clarity, sustainable access, transparent documentation and metadata, harmonised and standardised protocols;  identify potential barriers and enablers for translation of these R&I developments into practical and commercial digital tools and for the adoption by end-users (especially related to trust and transparency, and the needs of persons with disabilities such as accessibility of the information), as well as characterise remaining knowledge, training and/or advice gaps, and needs for policy feedback.    The projects under this topic are relevant to the EU policies related to the EU Vision for Agriculture and Food, the EU Action Plan for the Development of Organic Production [1] , Europe fit for the Digital Age, the Climate Adaptation Strategy, the Zero Pollution Action Plan, the Clean Air directives, the EU biodiversity strategy for 2030 and the European Water Resilience Strategy.  Proposals must implement the multi-actor approach, with a consortium based on a balanced mix of actors with complementary knowledge, including farmers, researchers, advisors, technology providers and business partners.  This topic requires the effective contribution of SSH disciplines and the involvement of SSH experts, institutions as well as the inclusion of relevant SSH expertise, in order to produce meaningful and significant effects enhancing the societal impact of the related research activities.  Proposals should address various farming systems/approaches, one of which should be organic farming.  Where appropriate, proposals should use and complement capacities and infrastructures created under the Digital Europe Program (incl. European Data Spaces, EDIHs) as well as the EURO HPC and EU AI Factory infrastructures. Proposals should also comply with existing EU framework and strategies, and build upon the concepts and solutions developed in other EU initiatives aimed to facilitate data sharing, such as the Common European Agricultural Data Space (CEADS).  Proposals are encouraged to engage in international cooperation and to build on the results of relevant projects funded under Horizon 2020 and Horizon Europe and ensure collaboration with relevant ongoing and forthcoming projects under the PRIMA and Agriculture of Data partnerships, the JRC and the European Soil Observatory (EUSO).  null   Activities are expected to achieve TRL 4-5 by the end of the project – see General Annex B. title: Advanced Digital Skills
description: Expected Outcome:    Deliverables:     Initiatives implemented for the target audience to collect knowledge on learning needs in the area of AI uptake in health.  Training programmes in the area of advanced digital skills for AI uptake in health, designed jointly by higher education institutions, VET providers, research organisations, businesses and other stakeholders in digital health, in collaboration with the network of AI-powered advanced screening centres.  Training catalogue with detailed course planning and timetable, regularly updated.  Final analysis of the completed training and the achievement level reached in improved skills.  A landing page integrated into the Digital Skills and Jobs Platform, showcasing existing and forthcoming education and training initiatives and promoting training offers to the relevant audience.    Objective:  The academic offer in the area of advanced digital technologies in the EU is still lagging behind other regions of the world, especially when compared to the United Kingdom or the United States [1]  even though the number of both bachelor’s and master’s programmes in the EU has increased through the years. Furthermore, apart from delivering excellent programmes in specific digital technologies, there is also a growing demand for interdisciplinary programmes to equip sector specialists with the digital skills to deploy and use advanced digital technologies.  The actions under this topic aim at tackling the lack of academic training offer in advanced digital skills in key digital areas, while triggering a new way of delivering education programmes and training, building partnerships between education and training providers, businesses and research across the EU, and supporting the digital skills necessary for the deployment of digital technologies in strategic sectors.   1 This represents an increase of 8% in the number of bachelor programmes and an increase of 14% in the number of master programmes in the area of advanced digital skills. The dataset by the Joint Research Centre on the ‘Academic offer of advanced digital technologies 2022-2023’ is available here:    JRC Data Catalogue - Dataset - European Commission       Scope:  This topic aims to expand the offer of education and training in Artificial Intelligence in health jointly designed between higher education and training institutions, research organisations and industry. The content must reflect the latest policy developments, notably the Apply AI Strategy [1]  and the European Health Data Space [2] . It should cover developments in and application of AI and related digital health technologies.  The target audience is healthcare professionals, as well as computer and data scientists, programmers, and software developers working in the healthcare sector. Trainings must reflect the learning needs of the target audience and will vary in depth and technical complexity to accommodate different levels of expertise and learning preferences. To this end, the proposed project(s) should design and deliver the trainings in cooperation with the Apply AI Strategy flagship “European network of AI-powered advanced screening centres” [3].   The training courses should be made available to members of the “European network of AI-powered advanced screening centres” at least quarterly. The training sessions and material should be available in English and other EU languages, considering the needs of the target audience that need to be established. The training catalogue and content should be adapted regularly, according to target audience feedback.  Whenever applicable, the projects should foster the use of the HealthData@EU infrastructure and other European health data infrastructures (Genomic Data Infrastructure, Cancer Image Europe, the European Virtual Human Twins advanced platform, ICU data space), explore synergies and build on relevant education and training activities developed and provided in the context of those initiatives, as well as in the relevant projects funded by EU4Health or Erasmus+ providing digital skills training for the health workforce [4].    1    https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/apply-ai        2    https://health.ec.europa.eu/ehealth-digital-health-and-care/european-health-data-space-regulation-ehds_en        3    https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/apply-ai     4    https://ec.europa.eu/info/funding-tenders/opportunities/portal/screen/opportunities/projects-details/43353764/101056563/ERASMUS2027

title: SPACE
description: Expected Outcome:  The topic encompasses actions within the scope of the co-programmed European Partnership on Globally Competitive Space Systems (‘Space Partnership’) in the areas of satellite communication (SatCom), Earth Observation (EO) and New Commercial Space Transportation Solutions and is part of cohesive activities in the domain of digital developments under the grand heading of “digitalisation for commercial space solutions”.  Digitalisation is a major enabler for enhancing the value of an End-to-End EO and SatCom system. Under the area of  Using Space on Earth  related to SatCom and EO, below this topic focusses on the  Low to Mid TRL level developments of key technologies  [1]  required to strengthen competitiveness in these domains with a dedicated focus on synergies between Earth observation and Satellite telecommunication technologies.  Projects are expected to contribute to one or several of the following outcomes:   Next generation Earth observation and SatCom payloads, technologies and processing means (on ground and in space);  Security of SatCom and EO services, supporting next-generation technologies for both ground and space commercial applications.     This will contribute to developing, deploying global, more flexible and reactive space-based services applications, to contribute to fostering the EU's space sector competitiveness, as stated in the expected impact of this destination.  Scope:  The areas of R&I, which needs to be addressed to tackle the above-mentioned expected outcomes are:   R&I on End-to-End SatCom Mission capabilities for increased robustness, energy efficient connectivity and compatibility with 5G & 6G waveforms such as constellation and network software management systems and optical communications, including both space and ground-based assets, and digital on-ground infrastructure to test and enhance operational efficiency;  R&I on building blocks and processes common to EO and SatCom systems allowing for in-orbit reconfigurability, faster data availability, on-board and on-ground smart computing and improved operation resilience.     Proposals are expected to promote cooperation between different actors (industry, SMEs, research institutions and infrastructures and academia) and consider opportunities to quickly turn technological innovation into commercial use in space.  It is expected that projects make use of existing EU technologies and/or building blocks, including at component level, contributing to EU non-dependence and strengthen competitiveness, and this should be clearly presented in the proposal. Furthermore, proposed activities should be complementary to H2020 and Horizon Europe funded projects, national activities and activities funded by the European Space Agency (ESA).  This topic contributes to the implementation of the European Partnership on ‘Globally Competitive Space Systems’ (GCSS).   In this topic, the integration of the gender dimension (sex and gender analysis) in research and innovation content should be addressed only if relevant in relation to the objectives of the research effort.  null   Activities are expected to achieve TRL 4-5 by the end of the project. The reference TRL definition is the ISO 16290:2013 applicable to the space sector. title: BATTERIER och MOBILITET
description: Förväntat resultat:  Projektresultaten förväntas bidra till samtliga följande förväntade resultat:   Utveckling av system som använder dataanalys i realtid för att dynamiskt reagera på störningar, vilket gör det möjligt för transport- och infrastrukturoperatörer att anpassa verksamheten snabbt och effektivt.  Utveckling av strategier för förebyggande underhåll som tillämpar innovativa generativa AI-lösningar och utnyttjar annan digital teknik för att förutse och förhindra fel på infrastruktur och utrustning.  Utarbetande av riktlinjer och verktyg för att stödja persontransportföretag och myndigheter för att säkerställa minimala störningar i oväntade och kritiska situationer och organisera simuleringar av nödsituationer i verkliga livet.  Införande av utbildningsprogram för transport- och infrastrukturoperatörer om hur man hanterar transportstörningar, inbegripet verktyg och katalog med beredskapsplanering för specifika transportstörningar.  Minskning av den genomsnittliga passagerarförseningen på korridornivå (minst 20 %) under planerade störningar, jämfört med referensscenariot, och av den tid (minst 40 %) som behövs från det att en åtgärdsplan tas fram till dess att den sprids till olika berörda parter (t.ex. transportföretag, passagerare, medborgare) under oplanerade och kritiska händelser, jämfört med referensscenariot.    Tillämpningsområde:  Passagerartransportsystem är en viktig del av stads-, förorts- och långdistansresor, underlättar konnektivitet, minskar trafikstockningar och stöder miljömässig hållbarhet. Dessa system står dock inför utmaningar som driftsstörningar, säkerhetsrisker och föränderliga passagerarkrav.  I samband med persontransporter avser resiliens ett transportsystems förmåga att absorbera störningar, upprätthålla sin grundläggande struktur och funktion och återhämta sig till en nödvändig servicenivå inom godtagbar tid och kostnad efter att ha påverkats av störningar. Det handlar om att genomföra åtgärder som säkerställer kontinuerlig drift, snabb återhämtning från oväntade händelser och anpassningsförmåga till förändrade omständigheter. Ökad resiliens är avgörande för att upprätthålla allmänhetens förtroende och säkerställa att transportsystemen fungerar smidigt, och den är en hörnsten i EU:s strategi för hållbar och smart mobilitet.  De föreslagna åtgärderna förväntas omfatta samtliga följande aspekter:   Utveckling och genomförande av åtgärder för att öka motståndskraften hos stads-, förorts- och långdistanstransportsystem.  Utnyttja digital teknik (t.ex. stordata, digitala tvillingar) och i synnerhet generativ och diskriminerande AI för att förutse och förutsäga utvecklingen av störningar och deras effekter, med planerings- och informationssystem i realtid för att minimera effekterna och möjliggöra snabbare återhämtning.  Användning av innovativ teknik för datainsamling och integrering av data från olika källor som underlag för beslutsfattande och optimering av strategier samt skapande av scenariobibliotek för olika omvälvande händelser och övervakning av genomförandet av åtgärdsplanerna.  Involvera myndigheter och aktörer i designprocessen för att skapa helhetslösningar som är användarvänliga och anpassade till deras behov.  Genomföra skydds- och säkerhetsbedömningar vid datatolkning, säkerställa att beslut baseras på objektiva faktorer och samtidigt undvika partiskhet.  Testa och validera ovanstående aspekter i verkliga användningsfall i multimodala transportkorridorer inom stads-, förorts- och långväga persontransporter med minst tre transportsätt per användningsfall (t.ex. bussar, tunnelbana, spårvagnar, tåg, bussar, trådbussar, färjor, delad mobilitet) på minst tre pilotplatser i olika medlemsstater och som återspeglar en mångfald av operativa, geografiska och tekniska sammanhang.    Förslagen uppmuntras att bygga vidare på resultaten från tidigare ansökningsomgångar om infrastruktur och transportresiliens (t.ex. HORIZON-CL5-2024-D6-01-11, MG-7-1-2017, HORIZON-CL5-2021-D6-01-09), multimodal trafikledning (t.ex. HORIZON-CL5-2022-D6-02-05, MG-2-11-2020), delad mobilitet och kollektivtrafik (t.ex. HORIZON-CL5-2022-D6-02-04, HORIZON-MISS-2021-CIT-02-02). Förslagen bör också vara förenliga med befintliga EU-ramar och EU-strategier och bygga vidare på de koncept och lösningar som utvecklats inom andra unionsinitiativ som syftar till att underlätta datadelning inom transportsektorn, såsom det europeiska dataområdet för mobilitet (EMDS). Särskilda ansträngningar bör göras för att säkerställa att de uppgifter som tas fram inom ramen för detta ämne är FAIR (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable and Re-usable).  null   Verksamheten förväntas uppnå teknisk mognadsgrad 6–7 vid projektets slut – se allmän bilaga B.

title: PRZESTRZEŃ
description: Oczekiwany wynik:  Temat ten obejmuje działania w ramach współprogramowanego europejskiego partnerstwa na rzecz globalnie konkurencyjnych systemów kosmicznych („partnerstwo kosmiczne”) w obszarach łączności satelitarnej (SatCom), obserwacji Ziemi (EO) i nowych komercyjnych rozwiązań w zakresie transportu kosmicznego i jest częścią spójnych działań w dziedzinie rozwoju cyfrowego pod wielkim tytułem „Cyfryzacja komercyjnych rozwiązań kosmicznych”.  Cyfryzacja jest głównym czynnikiem zwiększającym wartość kompleksowego systemu EO i SatCom. W obszarze  Wykorzystywanie przestrzeni kosmicznej na Ziemi  związanym z SatCom i EO poniżej temat ten koncentruje się na szybkim wzroście  elementów składowych poziomu od niskiego do średniego TRL dla kluczowych technologii   [1]  wymaganych do wzmocnienia konkurencyjności w tych dziedzinach.  Oczekuje się, że projekty przyczynią się do osiągnięcia jednego lub kilku z następujących rezultatów:   nowe komercyjne usługi i zastosowania możliwe dzięki zwiększonej cyfryzacji rozwiązań kosmicznych;  sprzyjanie konkurencyjnemu i zrównoważonemu europejskiemu sektorowi kosmicznemu;  umożliwienie europejskiemu przemysłowi kosmicznemu utrzymania znacznego udziału w globalnym rynku łączności;  Obserwacje Ziemi nowej generacji i ładunki użytkowe SatCom, technologie i środki przetwarzania (naziemne i kosmiczne);  bezpieczeństwo usług SatCom i EO, wspierających technologie nowej generacji zarówno w zastosowaniach komercyjnych naziemnych, jak i kosmicznych;  Lepszy dostęp do danych satelitarnych dzięki systemom interoperacyjnym.    Przyczyni się to do opracowania, wdrożenia globalnych, bardziej elastycznych i reaktywnych aplikacji usług kosmicznych, aby przyczynić się do zwiększenia konkurencyjności unijnego sektora kosmicznego, jak stwierdzono w oczekiwanym wpływie tego miejsca docelowego.  Zakres stosowania:  Obszary R&I, którymi należy się zająć, aby osiągnąć wyżej wymienione oczekiwane wyniki, to:   R&I w zakresie kompleksowych zdolności misji SatCom w odniesieniu do obecnej i przyszłej interoperacyjności sieci satelitarnych, w tym zarówno zasobów kosmicznych, jak i naziemnych, oraz cyfrowej infrastruktury naziemnej w celu przetestowania i zwiększenia efektywności operacyjnej;  R&I w zakresie urządzeń, podsystemów, aplikacji i usług obserwacji Ziemi, poprawy terminowości kompleksowego systemu obserwacji Ziemi oraz ulepszonej rozdzielczości, miniaturyzacji projektów przyrządów oraz technik i technologii cyfrowych w celu wsparcia operacji i harmonizacji umożliwiającej interoperacyjność między wieloma misjami obserwacji Ziemi;  R&I w zakresie elementów składowych i procesów wspólnych dla systemów EO i SatCom, takich jak optymalizacja wykorzystania zasobów systemowych, wysokowydajne przetwarzanie ładowności H/W w celu wspierania zdolności sieci kosmicznych, w tym poprawa zdolności łącza w dół i wykonywania zadań w ramach europejskiej infrastruktury, naziemne stacje radiowe i optyczne hybrydowe stacje naziemne do celów usług kotwiczenia oraz dostosowanie technologii kwantowych do zastosowań kosmicznych.    Wnioski mogą przyczyniać się do realizacji co najmniej jednego z powyższych obszarów badań i innowacji, jednak główny obszar, którego dotyczą, musi zostać jasno i jednoznacznie określony w tekście wniosku.  Oczekuje się, że wnioski będą promować współpracę między różnymi podmiotami (przemysłem, MŚP, instytucjami badawczymi i infrastrukturami oraz środowiskiem akademickim) oraz rozważą możliwości szybkiego przekształcenia innowacji technologicznych w komercyjne wykorzystanie w przestrzeni kosmicznej.  Oczekuje się, że w projektach wykorzystuje się istniejące technologie lub elementy składowe UE, w tym na poziomie komponentów, przyczyniając się do niezależności UE i wzmocnienia konkurencyjności, co należy jasno przedstawić we wniosku. Ponadto proponowane działania powinny uzupełniać projekty finansowane w ramach programu „Horyzont 2020” i programu „Horyzont Europa”, działania krajowe i działania finansowane przez Europejską Agencję Kosmiczną (ESA).  Temat ten przyczynia się do realizacji europejskiego partnerstwa na rzecz globalnie konkurencyjnych systemów kosmicznych (GCSS).  W tym temacie uwzględnianie aspektu płci (analiza płci i płci) w treści badań naukowych i innowacji należy rozpatrywać tylko wtedy, gdy jest to istotne w odniesieniu do celów działań badawczych.  Poziom gotowości technologicznej - poziom gotowości technologicznej oczekiwany od ukończonych projektów   Oczekuje się, że działania osiągną TRL 4-5 do końca projektu. Referencyjną definicją TRL jest norma ISO 16290:2013 mająca zastosowanie do sektora kosmicznego.
