title: 1.a ronda de convocatorias abiertas – Apoyo a las pymes del sector textil hacia una transición digital y ecológica
description: Enlace al portal de solicitud en línea:  https://ec.europa.eu/eusurvey/runner/FutureProofTextiles-1st-OpenCall      Objetivo de la convocatoria abierta:    Capacitar a 20 pymes del sector textil para navegar con éxito las «dobles transiciones» de la transformación digital y la sostenibilidad ecológica.      Apoyo:    Más allá de la subvención de cofinanciación de 60 000 EUR (50  000 EUR – subvención fija a tanto alzado, 10 000 EUR – autofinanciación requerida por las pymes),  FutureProofTextiles ofrece amplios recursos de creación de capacidades y creación de redes para ayudar a construir un ecosistema de pymes conectado:    Formación a    medida: Una media de 40 horas por pyme centrada en la transformación digital, los principios de la economía circular y la producción sostenible.   Mentoría    dedicada: Sesiones personalizadas de consultoría técnica y tutoría para hasta 6 pymes seleccionadas en función de necesidades específicas.   Materiales de acceso    abierto: Producción de 100 horas de currículos de capacitación escalables y guías de mejores prácticas para el sector textil en general.      Redes transfronterizas: Facilitación de la colaboración internacional para fomentar un ecosistema textil innovador.     (Se compartirán más detalles sobre estos servicios con las pymes seleccionadas).     Quién puede aplicar:      Tamaño de la empresa       Los solicitantes deben pertenecer a la categoría de PYME, de acuerdo con la Recomendación 2003/361/CE de la Comisión Europea*       Asociaciones Los clústeres y las organizaciones intermediarias no son elegibles, incluso si son pymes.      Cada solicitante debe representar a una única pyme, no a un consorcio de múltiples pyme.     Industria       Los solicitantes deben ser pymes que operen en la cadena de valor textil. Las pymes de sectores complementarios (por ejemplo, tecnología, maquinaria) también son elegibles, siempre que su innovación propuesta contribuya directamente a la cadena de valor textil. Las actividades deberán ajustarse a un código NACE pertinente (o equivalente nacional), como:   Fabricación    textil: C13.1, C13.2, C13.3, C13.9      Fabricación de prendas de vestir: C14.1, C14.3      Productos textiles y textiles técnicos: C15.12, C22.19      Reciclaje textil y circularidad: C38   Soluciones    digitales e innovadoras para el sector textil: J62, J63      Fabricación de maquinaria para la producción de textiles, prendas de vestir y cuero: C 28.94      Ubicación       Solo podrán presentar su candidatura las pymes legalmente establecidas en países que participen en el Programa para el Mercado Único. Esto incluye a los Estados miembros de la UE y a cualquier otro país asociado formalmente al PSM. Una lista completa de los países participantes se publica aquí: Lista de países participantes en el Programa para el Mercado Único     Lengua       La pyme solicitante debe tener al menos un miembro del personal que hable inglés y participará activamente en el proceso de implementación, manejando todas las necesidades de comunicación con el consorcio.      Normas de presentación:     Plataforma       Propuesta presentada en línea en la Plataforma de Encuestas de la UE. No se aceptarán otros medios. Formulario de solicitud     Lengua       Las propuestas deben estar escritas en inglés. Las presentaciones realizadas en cualquier otro idioma no serán evaluadas.      Límite de presentación    Las pymes    solicitantes podrán presentar hasta dos propuestas por ronda de convocatoria abierta (una en el marco de la transición ecológica y otra en el de las innovaciones digitales). A pesar de esto, cada pyme es elegible para recibir un máximo de una subvención en todo el programa.     Requisitos de la propuesta       La propuesta debe demostrar un nivel de preparación tecnológica (TRL) de 5 o superior.      Cumplimiento & Ética     Los solicitantes deben confirmar su pleno cumplimiento de todas las normas, incluida la ausencia de doble financiación y el conflicto de intereses, revisando y firmando los formularios obligatorios incluidos en la solicitud:     Elegibilidad de   la financiación y ausencia de formulario de declaración de conflicto de intereses      Formulario de declaración de PYME y elegibilidad      Guía paso a paso      Los solicitantes podrán presentar    una    propuesta de proyecto de transición ecológica y    otra    de proyecto de innovación digital. Tenga en cuenta que se debe presentar una solicitud por separado para cada uno.     Etapa 1: Verificar la elegibilidad     Revise los requisitos de elegibilidad a fondo para asegurarse de que su organización y proyecto califiquen para la financiación.     Etapa 2: Concept & Presupuestación        Consulte el  documento «Exhaustive     List of Eligible Activities and Eligible Costs» (Lista exhaustiva de actividades subvencionables y costes subvencionables).        Consulte el  documento «Necesidades    de las pymes en el sector textil»,   que ayuda al proceso de lluvia de ideas.      Haz una lluvia de ideas sobre tu propuesta. Al hacer una lluvia de ideas, tenga en cuenta que el período de implementación del proyecto es de 9 meses.       Redactar un proyecto inicial y elaborar un presupuesto global basado en los costes subvencionables. Definir claramente sus objetivos mediante el establecimiento de hitos específicos.      Etapa 3: Proyecto de respuestas        Prepare sus respuestas para cada sección del  documento «Plantilla    normalizada de formulario de solicitud»,   antes de iniciar la presentación en línea.      Etapa 4: Preparar documentos obligatorios     Complete y firme los siguientes formularios requeridos:       Complete el    documento   «Tablas con actividades, presupuesto, hitos y riesgos».   Tenga en cuenta que los hitos pueden estar sujetos a negociación si se selecciona la propuesta, y los solicitantes no serán evaluados en función de los hitos propuestos.      Rellene el    formulario «PYME y declaración de elegibilidad».         Rellene el    formulario «Solicitud de financiación y ausencia de declaración de conflicto de intereses».         Etapa 5: Complete el formulario en línea      Acceda al portal en línea – Encuesta de la UE para introducir sus respuestas. Recomendamos utilizar una conexión a Internet estable para evitar la pérdida de datos.     Etapa 6: Cargar archivos adjuntos     Adjunte todos los documentos obligatorios del paso 4 en sus respectivos campos de carga dentro del formulario.    Todos los documentos necesarios están disponibles para su descarga a través del portal de aplicaciones y a través de los puestos pertinentes en los proyectos LindeIn y la página ECCP.    profile.clustercollaboration.eu/profile/cluster-partnership-initiative/c9fcd533-bf23-4b23-bd18-adb2e57b37a4    https://www.linkedin.com/company/future-proof-textiles     También puede ponerse en contacto con: fpt.eu.helpdesk@gmail.com

title: Apoyo a la ejecución de la Misión contra el Cáncer
description: Resultado esperado:  Las propuestas en el marco de este tema deben tener por objeto obtener resultados orientados y adaptados a los siguientes resultados esperados y contribuir a ellos:   A través del Centro Digital Europeo para Pacientes con Cáncer (ECPDC), los pacientes y supervivientes de cáncer adolescentes y jóvenes, así como sus cuidadores, tienen acceso a herramientas y enfoques innovadores para reforzar su salud mental;  Los profesionales de la salud tienen acceso a herramientas innovadoras para monitorear y apoyar la salud mental de los pacientes y sobrevivientes de cáncer, así como de sus cuidadores  Los investigadores y los profesionales de la salud tienen acceso y utilizan datos confiables reportados por los pacientes para comprender mejor las necesidades de salud mental de los pacientes y sobrevivientes de cáncer y proporcionar una atención efectiva.    Ámbito de aplicación:  Como parte de sus actividades de participación ciudadana, la Misión de la UE contra el Cáncer ha puesto en marcha un diálogo con los jóvenes supervivientes de cáncer para comprender mejor las necesidades y los retos específicos a los que se enfrentan durante y después del tratamiento.  La salud mental se ha destacado sistemáticamente como una preocupación importante, destacando la importancia del acceso a un apoyo psicosocial de calidad, también a través de medios virtuales y digitales a lo largo de las diferentes etapas del viaje del paciente, en el momento del diagnóstico, durante y después del tratamiento.  La Comunicación sobre un enfoque global de la salud mental, adoptada por la Comisión Europea el 7 de junio de 2023  [1],  pide la creación de una plataforma para impulsar la salud mental de los jóvenes supervivientes de cáncer.  En línea con esta ambición, el objetivo general de este tema es desarrollar una plataforma en línea dirigida a los pacientes y sobrevivientes de cáncer de adolescentes y adultos jóvenes (AYA) (de 15 a 39 años, edad del primer diagnóstico) para abordar específicamente sus necesidades de salud mental, a lo largo de su viaje, en el momento del diagnóstico, durante y después del tratamiento. En particular:   La plataforma digital debe desarrollarse como un módulo que se integre plenamente en el Centro Digital Europeo para Pacientes con Cáncer, cuyo portal de información se encuentra actualmente en fase de desarrollo (proyecto EU-CIP  [2]).  Por lo tanto, deben establecerse vínculos claros con la PIC de la UE y desarrollarse soluciones para vincular los dos proyectos, incluidas las soluciones operativas y la sostenibilidad.  La plataforma debe incluir una combinación de características innovadoras personalizadas, basadas en pruebas e interactivas basadas en investigaciones de vanguardia para abordar las necesidades de salud mental de los pacientes y supervivientes de AYA  [3].  Deben considerarse tanto aspectos cognitivos (pensamiento, razonamiento, memoria, percepción, etc.), afectivos (depresión, ansiedad, etc.) como de cambio de comportamiento.  Debe demostrarse claramente el carácter innovador de las soluciones propuestas.  Se debe incluir compatibilidad multidispositivo (móvil, tableta, web) y soporte multilingüe para llegar a diversas poblaciones.  Las necesidades específicas y las posibles soluciones deben debatirse y desarrollarse en estrecha cooperación con los usuarios finales.  Del mismo modo, la eficacia de las soluciones propuestas para apoyar e impulsar la salud mental de los pacientes jóvenes con cáncer, los supervivientes y sus cuidadores debe demostrarse sometiéndolos a pruebas y validándolos por un número adecuado de usuarios finales, con diferentes tipos de cáncer y pertenecientes al grupo de edad destinatario.  Desarrollar, probar e integrar en la plataforma herramientas innovadoras para la recopilación y el análisis de medidas de resultados notificados por el paciente (PROM) y medidas de experiencias notificadas por el paciente (PREM) relevantes para la salud mental. Debe permitirse la extracción efectiva de datos de experiencias vividas para apoyar, por ejemplo, el desarrollo y la validación psicométricos, la modelización de riesgos y la creación conjunta de medidas psicológicas personalizadas de salud mental.  Por lo tanto, las herramientas deben desarrollarse y validarse en estrecha cooperación con los usuarios finales, incluidos los pacientes, los supervivientes, los profesionales sanitarios y los investigadores.  Desarrollar directrices armonizadas con el Espacio Europeo de Datos Sanitarios (EEDS) para notificar y depositar los datos pertinentes notificados por los pacientes recogidos con las herramientas anteriores. description: Expected Outcome:  Projects should contribute to all of the following expected outcomes:   Provide policymakers, education practitioners and citizens with a solid understanding of how social media, video gaming and other leisure uses of digital tools relate to the educational outcomes of young people, including through their impact on well-being and mental health.  Generate rigorous, policy-relevant evidence about policies and practices aiming to inform and regulate young people’s use of digital tools for non-educational purposes, such as smartphones, at school.  Develop actionable advice for policymakers and citizens about how to promote young people’s healthy use of digital tools for leisure, both at school and outside school.  Describe and quantify the relationships of using digital tools for leisure and communication with students’ motivation, study habits, attention span and concentration, time management, engagement, social integration and overall well-being.     Scope:  The increasing prevalence of digital devices in young people’s life has raised concerns about the potential impacts of the use of digital tools for leisure and communication on primary-, secondary- and higher education students’ well-being and educational outcomes [1] . “Digital distraction” is emerging inter alia as a potential threat to academic performance and several countries have started to regulate the use of smartphones at school.  There is still limited evidence on the interrelation between the use of digital tools for leisure in-school or out-of-school and educational performance, in both primary and secondary education, because most of the existing literature is purely correlational, or only focuses on effects on well-being. Moreover, most existing research is from extra-EU contexts, which may limit the transferability of findings to EU education and training systems.  Several interrelated research questions remain to be addressed, such as:   Which types of digital device use do pupils perform during school and do their digital activities differ depending on different contexts (i.e., during class, during breaks or between classes)?  How do different activities (e.g. playing games vs. chatting with a parent), on different devices, with different time durations of use, relate to students’ attention span and concentration as well as general school motivation?  How does frequent smartphone, social media use and other online leisure activities (such as video games) impact students’ attention span, concentration, memory and relational capacities?     How can schools, educators and parents balance the use of those tools to enhance, rather than hinder, educational performance and students’ well-being?  What is the potential for addiction when using digital tools and what are the decisive factors for this on the part of the design of tools on the one hand and on the part of the users on the other?  How can digital leisure activities contribute to skills development, such as problem-solving and digital literacy and what is the transferability of these skills into education? How do these benefits compare with potential harm?  What is the role of parents and educators in guiding digital leisure activities? Explore parental digital literacy and its impact on the use of digital devices by the youth.     Proposals should explore the complex, context-dependent ways in which different forms of digital leisure affect attention, motivation, creativity, learning habits, critical thinking, and socio-emotional skills. They should consider variations across age groups, socio-economic backgrounds, cultural contexts, and types of digital engagement and include students with disabilities.  Proposals should apply rigorous experimental and/or quasi-experimental methods for their analysis and could complement them with experience sampling research, survey research methods and qualitative research methods. Close cooperation with educational authorities, educational institutions and educators in analysing existing policies and practices is essential. Proposals should also include the opinions of young people and other relevant stakeholders, such as media literacy organisations, for example, in the form surveys, interviews, consultations, as part of the data collection. Proposals could apply interdisciplinary approaches (including from SSH disciplines), combining insights from economics, sociology, neurosciences, communication science (media psychology) and pedagogy. Clustering and cooperation with other selected projects under this call and other relevant projects are strongly encouraged.  [1] Cf. European Commission initiative on ‘A comprehensive approach to mental health’ or the call for evidence for an EU Action Plan Against Cyberbullying’.

title: BATERIAS E ENERGIA
description: Resultado esperado:  Espera-se que os resultados do projeto contribuam para todos os seguintes resultados esperados:   Ferramentas avançadas e seguras de IA frugal (energia, recursos, dados, eficiência em termos de custos e sustentabilidade) para operações de rede em tempo real (incluindo proteção), operações de mercado (se for caso disso) e capacitação dos consumidores em sistemas de energia distribuída.  Um ambiente de desenvolvimento de IA comprovado, integrado com a coluna vertebral digital atualizada do sistema energético e com aplicações de poupança de energia para os consumidores.  Capacidades ampliadas para a aprendizagem em nós periféricos e sistemas federados usando arquiteturas baseadas em agentes.  Um quadro de governação e um modelo operacional para a coluna vertebral digital alimentada por Gen(AI).    Âmbito de aplicação:  Com base em ações anteriores no âmbito do Horizonte Europa (por exemplo, a coluna digital do sistema energético no agregado 5, bem como as atividades de tratamento contínuo de dados em nuvem e periféricos e de IA no agregado 4) e do Europa Digital (Quadro de Referência Comum para as aplicações de consumo de energia em toda a UE, Espaço Comum de Dados Energéticos), prevê-se que os projetos:     Validar (local de produção e rede operacional) e dimensionar ferramentas e modelos de IA de fonte aberta (gerativa) de ponta especializados e seguros (e eficientes em termos energéticos e de recursos, eficientes em termos de dados e de custos, implantados localmente e sustentáveis) para a monitorização, o equilíbrio, a previsão e a capacitação dos consumidores de uma rede em tempo real (e do mercado, se for caso disso) num sistema energético distribuído.  Demonstrar um ambiente de desenvolvimento da IA no âmbito da coluna vertebral digital reforçada do sistema energético, incluindo o seu gémeo digital, que deve incorporar a funcionalidade do Quadro de Referência Comum para as aplicações de poupança de energia.  Protótipo e validação em escala da aprendizagem automática ao nível do nó periférico e federada ao nível do enxame numa arquitetura baseada em agentes, aproveitando novos mecanismos para reduzir os modelos de IA, bem como a aprendizagem incremental e de reforço.  Os resultados do projeto devem ser compatíveis com os princípios do Espaço Europeu Comum de Dados Energéticos e coerentes com as Orientações da UE para a Aplicação da IA e a Competitividade, assegurando que promovem a adoção da IA e a competitividade em consonância com as políticas da UE, bem como com as iniciativas da UE em matéria de digitalização do setor da energia.  Sempre que pertinente e possível, espera-se que os projetos selecionados utilizem as fábricas europeias de IA e as gigafábricas de IA.  Espera-se que os projetos selecionados, quando disponíveis, utilizem e desenvolvam normas europeias acordadas em comum e colaborem ativamente e contribuam para o trabalho das organizações de desenvolvimento de normas europeias estabelecidas e de facto e das comunidades e plataformas de fonte aberta.    Espera-se que os projetos selecionados contribuam para a iniciativa BRIDGE  [1]  e participem ativamente nas suas atividades. title: Accelerating Best Use of Technologies
description: Expected Outcome:  Expected outcomes and deliverables are:   Work strand 1:      Guidance for public authorities and healthcare providers to deploy, upgrade and operate digital health services and systems that support the rights of citizens and fulfil their obligations under the EHDS.  Maintenance and expansion of a community of public authorities and healthcare providers based on common guidance for services and systems aligned with the objectives of the EHDS. The community should build upon one or more existing communities.  Large-scale deployment of and/or capacity building for digital health services and systems that support the EEHRxF and the rights of citizens included in the EHDS.    Work strand 2:      A toolbox for data holders to support dataset description, data quality and utility labelling, and secondary use readiness in alignment with the EHDS.  Establishment or expansion of existing community of data holders with the objective of supporting peer exchange, reuse of good practices and alignment of approaches for the creation and maintenance of dataset descriptions and data quality and utility labels for secondary use under the EHDS.  Creation of dataset descriptions and data quality and utility labelling by data holders, such as public authorities and healthcare providers.  Integration of datasets descriptions in the datasets catalogues of health data access bodies.  Support to data holders in putting in place the organisational and technical arrangements required to make electronic health data available for secondary use under the EHDS, in line with applicable safeguards.    Work strand 3:      A training framework and training sessions to prepare service providers to support public authorities, healthcare providers and data holders in the implementation of the EHDS as described above, complementing and aligning with the work of the EEHRxF Support Centre, i2X Capacity Building for Secondary Use [1], and QUANTUM [2] .  A business model, including the uptake strategy, for service providers that can support the adoption of the EEHRxF, the uptake of services and systems compatible with the EHDS and the creation and maintenance of dataset descriptions and data quality and utility labels.  A community of trained service providers trained to support public authorities, healthcare providers and data holders in fulfilling requirements of the EHDS.    1 -    https://hadea.ec.europa.eu/calls-tenders/capacity-building-secondary-uses-health-data-european-health-data-space_en     2 -    https://quantumproject.eu/    Objective:  Regulation (EU) 2025/327 of the European Parliament and of the Council (‘The European Health Data Space (EHDS) Regulation’) [1] reinforces the rights for citizens to access and control their personal electronic health data and supports their freedom of movement by improving the cross-border exchange of such data to ensure continuity of healthcare. These rights include the right of natural persons or their representatives to access their personal electronic health data through electronic health data access services, the right to insert information in their own electronic health record (EHR), the right to rectification, the right to portability and the right to restrict access to their electronic health data. The rights also contribute to the achievement of the target of 100% of Union citizens having access to their electronic health records by 2030, as set in the Digital Decade policy programme.  For primary use, implementing these rights under the EHDS Regulation requires concrete action, capacity-building and training, to support the digital health community, particularly public authorities, healthcare providers, and service providers, particularly Small and Medium-sized Enterprises (SMEs), in the deployment of digital health services and systems that support these rights (across all the priority data categories) and that adopt the EEHRxF (European Electronic Health Record Exchange Format), taking into account the specific circumstances of different categories of stakeholders involved.  For secondary use, the EHDS Regulation requires health data holders, including public authorities and healthcare providers, to create and maintain a dataset description, following a health extension of the DCAT Application Profile [2] (currently under development), and, where applicable, a dedicated labelling for data quality and utility (also under development. These datasets descriptions and labels will need to be made available in the datasets catalogue of health data access bodies (HDABs).  The action is divided in  three objectives , each to be achieved through a separate work strand:   a) to build capacity of public authorities, healthcare providers to deploy services and systems that support the rights of natural persons under Chapter II of the European Health Data Space (EHDS) Regulation (primary use);  b) to build capacity of health data holders to improve quality of data, create the datasets description and label for electronic health data they hold and that is within the scope of the EHDS for secondary use;  c) to train service providers, particularly Small and Medium-sized Enterprises (SMEs), to support public authorities, healthcare providers and data holders in the implementation of the requirements set by the EHDS.   These objectives will be implemented through three work strands of a single project that will provide cascading funding to the third parties through a single call.  This action will foster a more efficient and interconnected healthcare ecosystem, supporting early adopters including at least public authorities, healthcare providers, health data holders and service providers to advance the implementation of the primary and secondary use requirements in the EHDS.   1    Regulation - EU - 2025/327 - EN - EUR-Lex     2    HealthDCAT-AP Release 5    Scope:  The selected project will manage a portfolio of individual grants across the three work strands by cascading funding mechanism, through financial support to third parties with the maximum amount of up to 120.000 euro per third party. The project consortium will be responsible for selecting, coordinating and monitoring the portfolio of cascaded grants across the three work strands and will ensure their coherent execution in line with the objectives, scope and deliverables defined in the Digital Europe Work Programme 2025-2027 without prejudice to the roles and responsibilities assigned to Health Data Access Bodies under the EHDS Regulation. Therefore, the consortium must demonstrate the ability to develop and execute this type of funding mechanism by involving participants with profound previous experience in this field.  The work of these projects will be implemented through three main work strands:      Work strand 1:  The consortium will provide guidance for public authorities and healthcare providers to deploy, upgrade and operate digital health services and systems that support the rights of citizens for primary use of their electronic health data and fulfil their obligations under the EHDS. The consortium will support, through the cascading funding mechanism, activities of public authorities and healthcare providers (e.g. hospitals, clinics, healthcare providers) to deploy digital health services and systems that support the rights of citizens included in the EHDS and the adoption of the EEHRxF, as well as to convert electronic health data into the EEHRxF. As part of the deployment, capacity building activities such as training for staff or reengineering processes can be included.   Work strand 2:  The consortium will develop a toolbox to support data holders in preparing electronic health data for secondary use in accordance with the EHDS. Through the cascading funding mechanism, it will support data holders to create and maintain dataset descriptions and, where applicable, data quality and utility labels for electronic health data falling within the scope of the EHDS. This strand will support data holders in publishing dataset descriptions and labels in the dataset catalogues operated by Health Data Access Bodies, thereby enabling data discoverability and access for secondary use. It will also support data holders in putting in place the necessary organisational and technical arrangements to make data available for secondary use under the EHDS, in line with applicable safeguards. Activities under this strand may include, where relevant, supporting data management practices, tooling and workflows, targeted IT deployment, staff training and process reengineering, insofar as these activities facilitate dataset description, cataloguing and secondary use readiness.   Work strand 3:  It will develop a training framework and conduct trainings for service providers to prepare them to support public authorities and healthcare providers to deploy digital health services and systems that support the rights of citizens included in the EHDS. It will also prepare them to convert health data held by public authorities and healthcare providers from various formats to the EEHRxF and vice-versa, and to deploy processes and services to enable such conversions, and to create and maintain dataset descriptions and the corresponding labelling for data quality and utility as foreseen in the EHDS for secondary uses of data.   This action is aimed at providing the necessary support, tools, and incentives in complementarity with other associated projects under Digital Europe Programme, EU4Health and Horizon Europe, such as i2X, MyHealth@MyHands, Xt-EHR, TEHDAS2, x-Share, SHAIPED. It should cover a large number of Member States and be deployed supporting all the priority data categories under EHDS. The action contributes to the eHealth Target of the Digital Decade Policy programme established by Decision (EU) 2022/2481 of the European Parliament and of the Council (the ‘DDPP Decision’) [1] through the implementation of EHR systems and digital health services and systems enabling access of citizens to their EHRs as well as contributing to the implementation of the European Data Union Strategy by increasing data discoverability and improved data quality.   1    https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dec/2022/2481/oj
